title: Assessing climate and socio-economic effects of agricultural credit policies: A case study of Brazil
description: Analysis of how directed agricultural credit programmes influence farm investment, productivity, rural labour markets, and land-use patterns, with implications for mitigation co-benefits and deforestation pressure.
methodology: Econometric assessment linking credit disbursement to farm-level productivity, employment, and land expansion; scenario comparison of credit allocation rules.
assumptions: Credit uptake responds to interest rate subsidies and eligibility rules
Productivity gains require complementary inputs (seeds, fertiliser, extension)
Land expansion is possible where tenure and market access allow
limitations: Results specific to Brazilian credit institutions and farm structure
Does not capture all indirect leakage effects
Uganda farm sizes and credit markets differ materially

sources.title: UNFCCC Katowice Committee of Experts on the Impacts of the Implementation of Response Measures (KCI)

nodes.label: Lower cost of capital for farms

outcomes.description: Rural labour demand rises with expanded production and seasonal harvesting
Agricultural output and downstream value-chain activity contribute to regional GDP
Yield per hectare improves where credit is paired with technical assistance
Pressure to convert natural land to agriculture where credit incentives favour expansion
Benefits may concentrate among larger farms with better access to credit markets
Mitigation potential from productivity gains vs. emissions from land conversion

trade_offs.positive_effect: Increased agricultural productivity and rural jobs
trade_offs.negative_effect: Reduced natural conservation area / biodiversity pressure
Credit access skewed toward commercial farms — equity gap widens

trade_offs.positive_effect: More space for real estate / development at forest margins
trade_offs.negative_effect: Less primary forest and carbon stock retention
